newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Coconut oil prices seen dipping on higher supply.
newsitem.headline: Coconut oil prices seen dipping on higher supply.

text.p: Coconut oil prices are expected to slide further this week on news of higher-than-expected exports from the Philippines in May and June, Manila vegetable oil traders said on Monday.
"We were expecting an average of 60,000 tonnes but it seemed like it was higher," said a senior Manila trader.

Trade group United Coconut Associations of the Philippines Inc said coconut oil exports between June 1 and 25 reached 121,950 tonnes, or more than three times the volume shipped in the same month last year.
A total of 40,543 tonnes of coconut oil were exported in June 1996.
"The preliminary export figures this month were bloated by two delayed shipments in May carrying at least 60,000 tonnes of oil," a senior trader at a Philippine oil mill.
Traders said they expect higher exports in the coming months due to prospects of better harvests.
One said, "I expect prices to shed as much as $20 per tonne this week."
UCAP said Philippine coconut oil buyers quoted $642.50 per tonne CIF for June/July shipment on Monday while sellers were at $651.25 per tonne.
Coconut oil stocks in Rotterdam dropped to 9,539 tonnes as of June 24 from the week-ago level of 13,229. "But we don't expect any aggressive buyers in the coming days," said one trader.
Four ships carrying 100,000 tonnes of coconut oil from Manila and Jakarta are expected to arrive in Rotterdam in two weeks.
